Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi Flood: Search, Rescue and Relief Response
Situation Report # 01
Date: 01 September 2026 Time: 09:00AM
This report has been prepared by the NDRRMA based on information received from DAO and District/National Emergency Operation Centers. It
summarizes the response actions undertaken for search, rescue, and relief management following the Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi flood situation.
Highlights
• A total of 5 districts are
affected, including 2
severely affected districts
(Rasuwa and Nuwakot) with
approximately 1.6 million
people impacted and 3
moderately affected
districts (Dhading, Gorkha,
and Chitwan).
• Deceased bodies 987 and
body parts recovered from
different districts along the
Bhotekoshi–Trishuli River
Basin, including Rasuwa,
Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha,
Nawalparasi East and West,
Tanahun and Chitwan.
• Missing individuals 3,916 have been reported across 62 districts of Nepal.
• Sucessfully rescued 253 foreign nationals.
• Through various operations 11,814 individuals have been rescued.
• Deployed 21,011 security personnel from national and international rescue teams, including teams from
Korea, China and India mobilized for joint search and rescue operations.
• 3,702 households, comprising a population of 14,461 (7,453 males and 7,008 females, including 3,650
children and 1,204 older persons), remain isolated in the two most severely affected local levels (Gosaikunda
and Amachhodingmo Rural Municipalities, Rasuwa), with road connectivity, electricity, and communication
services disrupted for up to six days since the incident, severely limiting access to essential services,
supplies, and emergency assistance.
• A total of 41 motorable bridges have been washed away, while an additional 4 bridges have been damaged.
Situation Overview
On 26 August 2026, a major ice–rock avalanche occurred in the upper Bhote Koshi watershed near the China–
Nepal border, approximately 20 km upstream of Rasuwagadhi. Preliminary analysis based on high-resolution
satellite imagery indicates that the event originated from a north-facing slope near the Lhende River, where an
estimated 1 km² section of rock-glacier material detached and rapidly moved downslope. The detached ice and
rock mass generated an ice–rock avalanche that entrained loose proglacial sediments along its downstream
path, transforming into a highly mobile sediment- and water-laden debris flow. Initial assessments suggest that
the resulting outburst flood in the upper watershed exceeded the magnitude of normal seasonal flooding by an
order of magnitude or more.
A seismic signal equivalent to a magnitude greater than 5 Mw earthquake was recorded near the Langtang/
Lirung area, close to the identified avalanche source zone. Subsequent analysis confirmed that the seismic signal

was generated by the large mass movement itself and
was not the triggering cause of the event. Following the
avalanche and debris-flood process, multiple temporary
lakes formed along the downstream flow path due to
channel blockage and sediment deposition. Satellite and
drone observations have confirmed that some of these
lakes have already drained; however, continued formation
of temporary impoundments remains possible due to
ongoing bank instability, channel obstruction and intense
rainfall. As a result, residual risks remain from sudden
river damming, lake breach floods, additional debris flows and secondary flooding events.
The event affected the Bhote Koshi–Trishuli–Narayani river corridor, a critical north–south transboundary
river system extending from the Tibet–Nepal border through Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha, Chitwan,
Tanahun and Nawalparasi. The corridor contains strategically important infrastructure, including the
Rasuwagadhi border crossing, customs and immigration facilities, major settlements, tourism routes, public
